(baseline 2014: more than 360) Progress/Status: Sewage pump stations have been rehabilitated, sewers cleaned, and a new outfall with screening facilities commissioned. Output: Financially and technical sustainability of KAJUR improved Indicator: By 2026:
KAJUR recovers 100% of its annual O&M cost of water and saltwater supply and sewerage systems through water tariff collection. (FY2011 baseline: 5% recovery) Progress/Status: A tariff framework has been developed and has been approved by the KAJUR Board in February 2021. The plan for implementation of the tariff framework was that this should start from Jan 2024. However, community outreach activities are required prior to this.
During the Nov 2025 mission, KAJUR advised that it recovers O&M costs for water and saltwater supplies, the sewage system and the electricity system through a single tariff collected for electricity. Data Source: KAJUR annual reports, project gender quarterly monitoring reports. Actual value:

Output: Secure and safe supplies of fresh water ensured Indicator: By 2026:
Standby 440KVA generator installed at the desalination plant. Progress/Status: Pending issue with interference with JICA's Solar PV project. Discussions ongoing.
Q2 2025 Update: Standby generator (2 units) to be procured in Q3 2025.
Q4 2025 update: Procurement did not push through due to COI issue as discussed with PPFD and OAI. Project team will revert to OAI, noting the current situation on the ground and the nature of relationships within RMI.
Q3 2025 Update: Procurement activities initiated, but likely to be cancelled due to potential COI issue between KAJUR and MEC. Data Source: Project progress reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Secure and safe supplies of fresh water ensured Indicator: By 2026:
The production of fresh water at the desalination plant runs and is maintained at a capacity of 1,600 m3/day. (Baseline 2014: 465 m3/day) Progress/Status: To be confirmed with KAJUR. As per OSMOFLO data (Jan 2024-Jun 2025 progress report, the desalination plant ran and maintained at an average capacity of 635 m3/day for the period Jan. 2023 to the June 2025. This is 40% of capacity and further progress to be confirmed during the Nov 2025 mission.
Q4 2025: the capacity in the indicator may not be achieved due to factors outside of the project's control (for example, electricity supply).
